gaps.uae_position: The human requirement is binding (26.7.2, licence 9.1) and Mizan enforces it. The CPR wants first-contact resolution (26.14.1) and bars the machine from the conversation (26.7.2); nothing joins the two: no text says what an automated channel must do at the moment a conversation becomes a complaint, or how fast the human must take over. The acknowledgement clock (26.13.3) names telephone, visit and written complaints, not chat or app, and a reference number is not a conversation.

gaps.gap: Standards gap, addressed to ITU. Mapped first: Mizan's stop at S2-3 sits at Y.3173 'Human and System' on the decision step (7.2, Table 7-1, p. 6: "a) Human; b) Human and System; c) System."), and its hand-over is Readiness 2.0 D9's inference-to-action latency in the other direction (p. 27: "inference-to-action latency: average time from first inference to human action"; there the AI alerts and the human acts). Readiness 2.0 also measures the human shaping the inference (D8, p. 25) and states that accountability of final decisions remains with humans (D10, p. 29). Mapped there, neither text measures when an acting agent must stop or how long the hand-over takes; ITU-T F.746.16 11.2 measures how often (a manual intervention rate, graded so that less intervention scores a higher level, no threshold), the opposite direction to a regulator's floor such as CPR 26.7.2; ITU-T F.748.67 CRR-003 measures the queue after the transfer, not the time to it. Y.3173 Table 7-2 NOTE 1 (p. 7) gives a human's order the highest authority ("decisions and execution instructions provided by a human being have the highest authority"); it never requires the system to ask. Y.3173 reproduces SAE J3016's levels in Appendix I (Table I.1), the request to intervene included, and carries no fallback dimension into its own Table 7-1.

gaps.line: the Cabinet schedule of licensee fines under Telecom Law 79 bis (2) is unpublished
gaps.gap: The Cabinet schedule of licensee violations and fines that Telecom Law 79 bis (2) promises (fines up to AED 10,000,000 a violation) is not published; the only published telecom fine schedule, Cabinet 57/2024, covers the Telemarketing Regulations. Until it exists, a CPR breach by an automated channel sits in the 79 bis (1) and licence 16.3.2 band, AED 50,000 to 200,000, doubled under licence 16.3.3 for repetition, a missed date or a material failure. The Cabinet has issued itemised schedules under three neighbouring laws (57/2024 telemarketing, 52/2024 trust services, 200/2025 digital trade); none under 79 bis (2). On 2026-11-02 the portal's Telecommunication, Technology and Space sector lists 12 instruments (14 in Arabic), none a schedule of telecom licensee fines; the Regulation Table of Decree-Law 3/2003 shows no records. The Cabinet has issued such a schedule for the space sector (Cabinet Resolution 206/2025, 'Regulations of Violations and Administrative Penalties... Space Activities'), not for telecommunications.
